newsitem.title: CANADA: Martin says rate cut due to finances, sees jobs.
newsitem.headline: Martin says rate cut due to finances, sees jobs.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin said the cut in the Bank of Canada's bank rate on Wednesday demonstrated that his budget deficit cuts were paying off, and they were translating into more employment.

"I think there is no doubt that the constant effort to clean up the balance sheet is paying off in lower interest rates, and that's going to translate into jobs and we're already seeing it," Martin told Reuters.
Asked if he foresaw further rate cuts, he said: "You'll have to ask the governor of the Bank of Canada."

Next Wednesday Martin will unveil his fiscal update, in which he is expected to show by how much he beat his deficit target for the 1995/96 fiscal year. He is under pressure from opposition politicians to reveal whether any tax cuts might be in the works.
